newsitem.title: USA: Buy Peru PDIs on further weakness - Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: Buy Peru PDIs on further weakness - Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Emerging markets investors should buy Peruvian PDI bonds if prices weaken further, according to a Morgan Stanley Group Inc analyst.

"We are of the view that a price of 55 with spread over (U.S.) Treasuries of 550 basis points is an attractive entry level," emerging markets analyst Jaime Valdivia Hernandez said in a report on Thursday.
Prices may dip because of the hostage crisis and delays in the closing of Peru's Brady operation, Valdivia said.
"Peruvian PDIs ... may weaken further in response to a market perception of widespread resurgence of terrorist activities and additional delays in the closing of its Brady operation," he said.
But the hostage-taking "is an isolated incident in our view (and) will not weaken economic reform," Valdivia added.
In addition, he said the Brady operation with commercial banks should close in late January or early February.

Peru will spend about $1.3 billion to finance a debt reduction of about $4.0 billion, Valdivia said. Peruvian reserves and participation of international organizations will cover most of that cost, he said.
"We believe financing has already been assembled," Valdivia said.
Peru's credit fundamentals and record of reform implementation should allow its debt to trade paralell with Panama's near term, Valdivia added.
Inflation in Peru declined to about an 11 percent rate by the end of 1996 from 11,000 percent in the third quarter of 1990, Valdivia pointed out.
The government initiated strong economic policies in 1990.
"Monetary policy has been successful in reducing inflation while effectively implementing open market operations to sterilize large capital inflows," he said.
Privatization of public-sector enterprises has attracted foreign investment, improving Gross Domestic Product, he said.
